facts.text: Allen was founded in 1872 by the Houston and Texas Central Railway and named after railroad promoter Ebenezer Allen.
In 1874 the same year the dam was built, the first successful train robbery in Texas allegedly took place at Allen Station while the train stopped for water.
Allen’s historic water station bridge and the surrounding gated foundation once housed a water tower and pump house, now a walking path with views of the dam.
The Allen Public Library began in 1967 when three ladies started it in a rent‑free room, and today it holds over 147,000 volumes.
Allen Station Park offers a baseball field, playground, and wake park, making it a hub for family recreation in the city.
